21.name: Fonds 21
21.what: A Dutch fund in Utrecht set up in 1998 by SNS REAAL, independent since that group's nationalisation in 2013.
21.money: Stichting Beheer SNS REAAL supplies its budget, €12 million in donations for 2026.
21.arts: It funds art, culture and education projects for young people aged 12 to 30.

aatoserkko.name: Jane and Aatos Erkko Foundation
aatoserkko.what: A private Finnish foundation set up in Helsinki in 2002 by the newspaper publisher Aatos Erkko and his wife Jane, mainly to fund research in technology, economics and medicine.
aatoserkko.money: Returns on Sanoma shares Aatos Erkko left it in 2012, worth about 700 million euros, which made it Sanoma's largest shareholder.
aatoserkko.arts: It also supports arts and culture, and gave grants of 45.2 million euros across all its fields in 2020.

adjarastamba.name: Adjara Group
adjarastamba.what: A Georgian hospitality holding founded in Tbilisi in 2010 by the entrepreneur Temur Ugulava, who died in 2026; its brands include Rooms Hotels, Stamba and Fabrika.
adjarastamba.money: Revenue from its hotels, restaurants, bars, co-working offices and event spaces in Georgia; the group employs about 1,700 people.

aerok.name: Aero K
aerok.what: A South Korean low-cost airline founded on 18 May 2016, flying since April 2021 from Cheongju International Airport; its parent is Aero K Holdings (Daemyung Chemical).
aerok.money: Passenger fares on its scheduled routes from Cheongju, flown with a fleet of nine aircraft.

aesop.name: Aesop
aesop.what: An Australian cosmetics brand founded in 1987 by the hairdresser Dennis Paphitis in Armadale, Melbourne; headquartered in Collingwood, Victoria, and owned by L'Oréal since 2023.
aesop.money: Sales of its skincare, haircare and fragrance products, as a subsidiary of L'Oréal.

afac.name: Arab Fund for Arts and Culture
afac.what: An independent non-profit founded in 2007 by Arab cultural activists that gives grants to artists, writers, researchers and cultural groups across the Arab region; based in Beirut.
afac.money: Donations, mainly from businesspeople and organisations in the Arab region, plus individual Friends and partner foundations and companies.
afac.arts: From 2007 to 2021 it raised slightly more than US$47 million and gave almost US$36 million in grants.

afd.name: Agence française de développement
afd.what: A French public financial institution, founded by Charles de Gaulle in 1941 as the Caisse Centrale de la France Libre, that finances development projects for the French state.
afd.money: Bonds it issues on the capital markets fund its loans; six of its board members represent French ministries.

ag2rlamondiale.name: AG2R La Mondiale
ag2rlamondiale.what: A French social protection and insurance group run jointly by employers and unions and as a mutual; La Mondiale was founded in 1905 by seven northern industrialists.
ag2rlamondiale.money: Supplementary pensions, provident and health insurance, life insurance and savings: revenue of €13.1 billion in 2025.

agencyforculturalaffairsjac|Japan.name: Agency for Cultural Affairs, Government of Japan
agencyforculturalaffairsjac|Japan.what: A special body of Japan's Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology, set up in 1968 to promote arts and culture, with its main offices in Kyoto since 2023.
agencyforculturalaffairsjac|Japan.money: Japan's national budget through the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology; its budget was 107 billion yen in 2026.
agencyforculturalaffairsjac|Japan.arts: Its divisions protect the nation's cultural properties and oversee the Japan Arts Council.

ahlstrmkiinteisttoy.name: A. Ahlström Kiinteistöt Oy
ahlstrmkiinteisttoy.what: The real estate subsidiary of A. Ahlström Oy, a Finnish family investment company; it owns and maintains Villa Mairea and runs the Ahlström Estate in Noormarkku.
ahlstrmkiinteisttoy.money: Its parent's investments in industry, real estate and forest; the companies A. Ahlström owns had about EUR 5.5 billion of revenue in 2025.

aig.name: American International Group, Inc.
aig.what: An American multinational insurance company founded in Shanghai on 19 December 1919 by Cornelius Vander Starr, now headquartered in New York City.
aig.money: Premiums and investment income from commercial and personal property, casualty, liability and specialty insurance; revenue was US$26.77 billion in 2025.
aig.address: 1271 Avenue of the Americas, New York, NY 10020

ajuntamentdebarcelona.name: Ajuntament de Barcelona
ajuntamentdebarcelona.what: The municipal government of Barcelona, elected every four years since 1979 and led by mayor Jaume Collboni; seated in the Casa de la Ciutat.
ajuntamentdebarcelona.money: The city's municipal budget: 4,180 million euros for 2026.

ako.name: AKO Foundation
ako.what: A London charitable foundation set up in 2013 by Nicolai Tangen, founder of the hedge fund AKO Capital, who left its board in 2020.
ako.money: Gifts from Nicolai Tangen, who in 2020 gave it substantially all of his partnership interest in AKO Capital and other investment assets.

alcaldademedelln.name: Alcaldía de Medellín
alcaldademedelln.what: The executive government of the Special District of Medellín, Colombia, a city of 2,427,129 people led by mayor Federico Gutiérrez; the city owns the utility company EPM.
alcaldademedelln.money: The district budget, funded by local taxes such as property and business tax; budgeted revenue grew to 12.90 trillion pesos for 2026.

alexanders.name: Alexander S. Onassis Public Benefit Foundation
alexanders.what: A private foundation set up in Vaduz, Liechtenstein, in 1975 under the will of the shipowner Aristotle Onassis, in memory of his son Alexander.
alexanders.money: Profits of the Onassis Business Foundation, its holding for maritime transport and real estate, formed from half of Aristotle Onassis's estate.
alexanders.arts: It endows Greek studies chairs at universities and runs Onassis USA, its New York affiliate based in the Olympic Tower on Fifth Avenue.

alexandertutsek.name: Alexander Tutsek-Stiftung
alexandertutsek.what: A non-profit foundation for art and engineering science, set up in Munich in 2000 by Alexander Tutsek and his wife Eva-Maria Fahrner-Tutsek, with its seat in Munich-Schwabing.
alexandertutsek.money: The fortune of Alexander Tutsek (1927 to 2011), previous shareholder of the Refratechnik Group, a Munich maker of refractory products for cement and steel plants.
alexandertutsek.arts: It collects glass sculpture and modern photography, holds exhibitions at its Schwabing headquarters and gives the C/O Berlin Talent Award to young photographers.

aliph.name: ALIPH Foundation
aliph.short: International Alliance for the Protection of Heritage (ALIPH)
aliph.what: A Geneva foundation set up in March 2017 at the initiative of France and the United Arab Emirates to protect heritage, with the immunities of an intergovernmental organisation.
aliph.money: Contributions from states including France, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Morocco, Luxembourg, China and Cyprus, plus the Mellon Foundation, the Getty and private donors.

alkenmaes.name: Brouwerij Alken-Maes
alkenmaes.what: A Belgian brewery formed in 1988 by merging the Maes brewery at Kontich-Waarloos with Cristal-Alken at Alken, headquartered in Mechelen and owned by Heineken.
alkenmaes.money: Beer sales, with profits going to its owner, the Dutch brewer Heineken.

allagash.name: Allagash Brewing Company
allagash.what: A craft brewery founded in Portland, Maine, in 1995 by Rob Tod, who owns it; it specialises in Belgian-style beers.
allagash.money: Beer sales: it was the Maine craft brewery with the highest sales volume in 2024 and brewed 94,743 barrels in 2017.

allies.name: Allies and Morrison LLP
allies.what: A London architecture and urban planning practice founded in 1984 by Bob Allies and Graham Morrison, with studios in Cambridge, Manchester, Dublin, Jeddah and Toronto.
allies.money: Fees from architecture, urban planning and consultancy commissions, much of it repeat work for long-term clients.

altum.name: JSC Development Finance Institution Altum
altum.what: A Latvian state-owned development finance company set up on 27 December 2013 by merging three state institutions; the finance, economics and agriculture ministries hold its shares.
altum.money: Latvian state and EU funds for the support programmes it runs, plus money it raises from international institutions and capital markets.

americaforbulgaria.name: America for Bulgaria Foundation
americaforbulgaria.what: An independent American philanthropic foundation working in Bulgaria, founded in 2008 as successor to the Bulgarian-American Enterprise Fund, a USAID investment fund set up under the 1989 SEED Act.
americaforbulgaria.money: A $400 million endowment descended from the Bulgarian-American Enterprise Fund, which US tax money financed; it gives about $20 million a year.

americanfriendsofisraelmuseumraisedover.name: American Friends of the Israel Museum
americanfriendsofisraelmuseumraisedover.what: A New York non-profit, tax-exempt since May 1972, that raises money in the United States for the Israel Museum in Jerusalem.
americanfriendsofisraelmuseumraisedover.money: Donations: in 2024 contributions were $11.8 million of its $15.9 million revenue, with $3.4 million in investment income.

ammodo.name: Stichting Ammodo
ammodo.what: A Dutch foundation set up in Amsterdam in 2011 that funds visual and performing arts, science and architecture.
ammodo.money: Mainly donations from the Inphykem Foundation, former sole owner of the pension insurer Optas, which it sold to Aegon in 2007.
ammodo.arts: Ammodo Art supports new visual and performing arts productions and development programmes with partner institutions.

amosanderson.name: Amos Andersons fond rf
amosanderson.what: A Finnish association founded in 1940 by the businessman and newspaper publisher Amos Anderson, renamed from Föreningen Konstsamfundet in 2025, based in Helsinki.
amosanderson.money: The fortune Amos Anderson bequeathed to it as sole legatee, held in investments and in Hufvudstadsbladet, the Swedish-language newspaper it wholly owns.
amosanderson.arts: It funds fine arts, publications, music and theatre for Swedish-speaking Finns and runs the Söderlångvik museum in Anderson's former summer home in Dragsfjärd.

ampersand.name: The Ampersand Foundation
ampersand.what: A UK grant-making charity for the visual arts founded in 2011 by the collector Jack Kirkland, a director and shareholder of the Bowmer + Kirkland group.
ampersand.money: Donations from founder Jack Kirkland, including £319,744 in 2024-25 from his 2003 family settlement, plus investment income.
ampersand.arts: Its biennial Ampersand Foundation Award gives a Plus Tate member institution the funds for its director's or curator's chosen project.
ampersand.address: Third Floor, 21 Conduit Street, London W1S 2XP

amsterdamforarts.name: Stichting Amsterdams Fonds voor de Kunst
amsterdamforarts.what: A private-law foundation that distributes Amsterdam's arts subsidies, listed in the Dutch register of organisations with government involvement, based at Pakhuis de Zwijger in Amsterdam.
amsterdamforarts.money: The City of Amsterdam's arts budget: the mayor and aldermen adopt its grant schemes within the city's Kunstenplan 2025-2028.
amsterdamforarts.arts: It gives four-year and project subsidies to Amsterdam arts organisations and makers, and awards the Amsterdamprijs voor de Kunst.

amsterdamsvoordekunst.name: Amsterdams Fonds voor de Kunst
amsterdamsvoordekunst.what: Amsterdam's arts fund, set up in 1972 to award the city's arts commissions and prizes, managing part of the municipal arts subsidy independently.
amsterdamsvoordekunst.money: The Municipality of Amsterdam, which funds it to carry out the city's Kunstenplan arts policy.
amsterdamsvoordekunst.arts: It runs multi-year subsidies under the Kunstenplan 2025-2028, one-off project grants and the Amsterdam Prize for the Arts.
amsterdamsvoordekunst.address: Pakhuis de Zwijger, Piet Heinkade 179, 1019 HC Amsterdam

andywarholforvisualarts.name: The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts
andywarholforvisualarts.what: A New York foundation set up in 1987 under Andy Warhol's will, which acts as the artist's estate and makes grants to the visual arts.
andywarholforvisualarts.money: An endowment built from Warhol's estate, sales of his works through Christie's and fees for licensing his images.
andywarholforvisualarts.arts: It has given over $300 million in cash grants to more than 1,000 arts organisations and donated 52,786 works to 322 institutions.
andywarholforvisualarts.address: 65 Bleecker Street, 7th Floor, New York, NY 10012

annenbergtrustatsunnylands.name: The Annenberg Foundation Trust at Sunnylands
annenbergtrustatsunnylands.what: A not-for-profit trust that owns and runs Sunnylands, the 200-acre Rancho Mirage winter estate of Walter and Leonore Annenberg, as a retreat for world leaders and a public site.
annenbergtrustatsunnylands.money: Returns on the Annenberg fortune, made publishing TV Guide, The Philadelphia Inquirer and Seventeen; revenue was $40.5 million in the year to June 2025.
annenbergtrustatsunnylands.arts: It holds the Sunnylands Collection of modern sculpture by Rodin, Giacometti, Arp and Agam, and runs public programmes on culture, music and film.
annenbergtrustatsunnylands.address: 37977 Bob Hope Drive, Rancho Mirage, California

anschutz.name: Anschutz Foundation
anschutz.what: A private foundation in Denver, tax-exempt since 1984, through which the billionaire Philip Anschutz makes grants.
anschutz.money: Dividends and asset sales on net assets of US$1.65 billion (fiscal 2024); Anschutz's fortune comes from oil, railroads and entertainment.

aon.name: Aon plc
aon.what: A professional services firm created in 1982 when Patrick Ryan's Ryan Insurance Group merged with Combined Insurance Company of America; corporate seat in Dublin, operations run from London.
aon.money: Fees and commissions from insurance and reinsurance brokerage and from risk, health and retirement consulting; revenue was US$15.70 billion in 2024.

appliedmaterialstaiwan.name: Applied Materials Taiwan
appliedmaterialstaiwan.what: The Taiwan subsidiary of Applied Materials, Inc., the US semiconductor and display equipment maker founded in 1967 in Santa Clara, California; it has sites in Hsinchu, Tainan and elsewhere.
appliedmaterialstaiwan.money: Sales and servicing of chip and display manufacturing equipment; the parent's revenue was US$34.446 billion in 2026.

aqualand.name: Aqualand
aqualand.what: An Australian luxury property, hospitality and investment group established in Sydney in 2014 and started by its managing director Jin Lin.
aqualand.money: Sales and leasing of its Sydney residential, commercial and mixed-use developments, such as Central Barangaroo, plus its AL Capital funds and Etymon Projects hospitality arm.

arabforarts.name: Arab Fund for Arts and Culture
arabforarts.what: An independent non-profit foundation set up in 2007 by Arab cultural activists and based in Beirut, supporting artists, writers and organisations across the Arab region.
arabforarts.money: Gifts from individual donors through its Friends of AFAC circle, and grants and sponsorship from foundations, companies and cultural institutions.
arabforarts.arts: It awards about 250 grants a year across seven programmes, including performing arts, visual arts, documentary film, music and writing.

arabpotash.name: Arab Potash Company
arabpotash.what: A Jordanian mining company founded in 1956 as a pan-Arab venture, based in Amman and the Arab world's sole potash producer; China's SDIC Mining bought 28% in 2018.
arabpotash.money: Sales of potash and derivatives harvested from the Dead Sea; net profit after tax and mining royalties was about JOD 173 million in 2025.

arpels.name: Van Cleef & Arpels
arpels.what: A Paris jewellery house founded in 1896 by Alfred Van Cleef and Salomon Arpels, now part of the Swiss luxury group Richemont.
arpels.money: Jewellery and watch sales for its owner Richemont, the luxury holding company Johann Rupert founded in 1988.
arpels.arts: Dance Reflections by Van Cleef & Arpels, launched in 2020, supports the creation and promotion of dance works and dance education.

art.name: National Art Collections Fund
art.what: An independent UK membership charity organised in 1903 by the activist Christiana Herringham to help public museums acquire art; based in London.
art.money: Subscriptions from its 142,000 members, who buy the National Art Pass, plus trusts, foundations and donors; it takes no government or National Lottery money.
art.arts: Since 1903 it has helped bring over 860,000 works of art into UK public collections.
art.address: 2 Granary Square, King's Cross, London N1C 4BH

artbridges.name: Art Bridges Foundation
artbridges.what: A US nonprofit founded in 2017 by Alice Walton that funds exhibitions, collection loans and programmes of American art with more than 400 partner museums.
artbridges.money: Alice Walton's philanthropy: she founded it and leads its board, and she is heiress to the Walmart fortune of her father Sam Walton.

artjameel.name: Art Jameel
artjameel.what: An independent arts organisation set up in 2003 as part of Community Jameel, the philanthropy of the Saudi Jameel family, with centres in Jeddah and Dubai.
artjameel.money: The Jameel family, owners of Abdul Latif Jameel, a Jeddah group founded in 1945 that has distributed Toyota cars in Saudi Arabia since 1955.
artjameel.arts: It partnered with the Victoria and Albert Museum in London in 2003.

artscouncilengland|UK.name: Arts Council England
artscouncilengland|UK.what: England's national development agency for the arts, museums and libraries, set up by Royal Charter in 1994 as an arm's length body of the Department for Culture, Media and Sport.
artscouncilengland|UK.money: UK government grant-in-aid through the culture department and National Lottery proceeds: £578,077,000 and £250,259,000 respectively in 2024-25.
artscouncilengland|UK.arts: It took over the Museums, Libraries and Archives Council in 2011 and has distributed lottery money to the arts since 1994.
artscouncilengland|UK.address: 2nd Floor, The Hive, 47 Lever Street, Manchester M1 1FN

artscouncilni|UK.name: Arts Council of Northern Ireland
artscouncilni|UK.what: Northern Ireland's arts development and funding agency, founded in 1964 and a non-departmental public body of the Department for Communities.
artscouncilni|UK.money: Exchequer funding from the Department for Communities and National Lottery money, which it distributes to artists and arts organisations.
artscouncilni|UK.address: The MAC, 10 Exchange Street West, Belfast BT1 2NJ

artscouncilofnorthernireland|UK.name: Arts Council of Northern Ireland
artscouncilofnorthernireland|UK.what: Northern Ireland's arts development and funding agency, founded in 1964 and a non-departmental public body of the Department for Communities.
artscouncilofnorthernireland|UK.money: Exchequer funding from the Department for Communities and National Lottery money, which it distributes to artists and arts organisations.
artscouncilofnorthernireland|UK.address: The MAC, 10 Exchange Street West, Belfast BT1 2NJ

artscouncil|Ireland.name: The Arts Council / An Chomhairle Ealaíon
artscouncil|Ireland.what: Ireland's national government agency for funding, developing and promoting the arts, established in 1951.
artscouncil|Ireland.money: The Irish state, which channels its arts funding to artists and arts organisations through the council.

artsqueensland.name: Arts Queensland
artsqueensland.what: The arts agency of the Queensland Government, a service area of the state Department of Education, based in Brisbane.
artsqueensland.money: The Queensland state budget: the arts portfolio received A$420.7 million for the first year of the Time to Shine strategy (2025).

atuge.name: Association des Tunisiens des Grandes Écoles
atuge.what: A non-profit, independent and non-political association of Tunisian graduates of the French grandes écoles, created in 1990, with branches in Tunis, Paris, the United Kingdom and Shanghai.
atuge.money: Membership dues from its more than 8,000 members worldwide.

aucklandcouncil|New Zealand.name: Auckland Council
aucklandcouncil|New Zealand.what: The unitary local and regional government of the Auckland Region, formed in 2010 by merging seven territorial authorities and one regional council.
aucklandcouncil|New Zealand.money: The council group reported NZ$8.7 billion in revenue in 2025/26, which also funds its council-controlled organisations.

augustinusfonden.name: Augustinus Fonden
augustinusfonden.what: A Danish commercial foundation set up in 1942 by Chr. Augustinus Fabrikker at the initiative of tobacco manufacturer Ludvig Augustinus; based in Copenhagen.
augustinusfonden.money: Chr. Augustinus Fabrikker, its wholly owned investment company, which grew from a 1750 tobacco mill and still holds about 25% of Scandinavian Tobacco Group.
augustinusfonden.arts: In 2021 it gave DKK 399 million, of which DKK 284 million went to art and culture.

axaforexhibitions.name: AXA
axaforexhibitions.what: A French multinational insurance company listed on Euronext Paris, with roots in an insurer founded in Rouen in 1817; Claude Bébéar's group took the AXA name in 1985.
axaforexhibitions.money: Premiums and investment income from property, casualty, health and life insurance, savings and pensions; revenue was €115.5 billion in 2025.

bahr.name: Advokatfirmaet BAHR AS
bahr.what: A Norwegian commercial law firm established in 1966, with 77 partners, more than 300 employees and offices in Oslo, Bergen, Tromsø, Copenhagen and Stockholm.
bahr.money: Legal fees from commercial clients and public sector organisations.

bailletlatour.name: Fonds Baillet Latour
bailletlatour.what: A Belgian foundation created by Alfred de Baillet Latour (1901 to 1980), the last male heir of his family, that funds health, education, culture, environment and Olympic sport.
bailletlatour.money: Its holding in the brewer AB InBev: 5,485,415 shares (0.27 percent) in 2019, held through the Stichting Fonds InBev Baillet Latour.
bailletlatour.arts: Since 2000 it has paid for the safeguarding, restoration and display of historic sites and artworks in Belgium.

bancatransilvania.name: Banca Transilvania S.A.
bancatransilvania.what: Romania's largest bank, founded in Cluj-Napoca on 16 February 1993 by 46 local entrepreneurs with US$2 million of capital.
bancatransilvania.money: Retail, corporate and investment banking; it held about 23% of Romanian banking assets in 2026 and has no majority shareholder.

banquenationale.name: Banque Nationale du Canada
banquenationale.what: Canada's sixth-largest commercial bank, created by an act of 4 May 1859 and headquartered in Montreal; it is the largest bank in Quebec.
banquenationale.money: Personal and commercial banking and wealth management, with 59% of revenue from Quebec in fiscal 2017.

basellandschaft.name: Kanton Basel-Landschaft
basellandschaft.what: A Swiss canton, traditionally the half-canton paired with Basel-Stadt, its urban counterpart, with its capital at Liestal.
basellandschaft.arts: Under the culture agreement its parliament approved in January 2020, it pays Basel-Stadt 9.6 million Swiss francs a year from 2022.

baselstadt|Switzerland.name: Kanton Basel-Stadt
baselstadt|Switzerland.what: The Swiss canton made up of Basel, Riehen and Bettingen, the smallest canton by area.
baselstadt|Switzerland.money: The cantonal budget, from which its culture department pays four-year operating grants to institutions, with an annual contribution from Basel-Landschaft.

bcartscouncil|Canada.name: British Columbia Arts Council
bcartscouncil|Canada.what: An agency of the Province of British Columbia created in 1995 under the Arts Council Act; based in Victoria.
bcartscouncil|Canada.money: The British Columbia provincial budget, through the Ministry of Tourism, Arts, Culture and Sport.
bcartscouncil|Canada.arts: In the year to 31 March 2018 it gave over C$24 million in awards, grants and scholarships in 225 communities.
bcartscouncil|Canada.address: 2nd Floor, 800 Johnson Street, Victoria, B.C. V8W 1N3

belfastcitycouncil|UK.name: Belfast City Council
belfastcitycouncil|UK.what: The local authority for Belfast, Northern Ireland's largest city, with 60 councillors who meet at Belfast City Hall.
belfastcitycouncil|UK.money: The district rate on Belfast homes and businesses, which councillors set each year, raised by 4.48 per cent for 2026/27.
belfastcitycouncil|UK.arts: Its Community Festivals Fund gives local groups grants of £2,500 to £10,000 for community festivals.

bengal.name: Bengal Group Ltd.
bengal.what: A Dhaka business group chaired since the mid-1970s by Abul Khair Litu, who set up the Bengal Foundation arts trust in 1986.
bengal.money: Abul Khair Litu's businesses, begun in the early 1970s; he co-founded AB Bank, Bangladesh's first private bank, in 1981.
bengal.arts: The Bengal Foundation, a private trust funded by the Bengal Group, has run international art camps since 1999.
bengal.wrong_match: Britto Arts Trust names the Bengal Foundation, not the company; Litu's Bengal Group is a different firm from Morshed Alam's Bengal Group of Industries.

berlinsenate|Germany.name: Senat von Berlin
berlinsenate|Germany.what: The executive of the city-state of Berlin, made up of the Governing Mayor and up to ten senators, meeting weekly at the Rotes Rathaus.
berlinsenate|Germany.money: The Berlin state budget, adopted as a two-year budget, now for 2026 and 2027.

bnkbusanbank.name: BNK Busan Bank
bnkbusanbank.what: A South Korean regional bank founded in 1967 and based in Busan, part of BNK Financial Group, launched in 2011 as BS Financial Group.
bnkbusanbank.money: Retail banking and foreign exchange through about 229 branches in Korea.

bnpparibasfortis.name: BNP Paribas Fortis
bnpparibasfortis.what: A Belgian bank created in May 2009, when the French group BNP Paribas bought 75% of Fortis Bank from the Belgian Federal Participation and Investment Company.
bnpparibasfortis.money: Banking in Belgium and abroad as a subsidiary of BNP Paribas.

boghossian.name: Boghossian Foundation
boghossian.what: A foundation created in 1992 by the jeweller Robert Boghossian and his sons Jean and Albert, of Armenian origin, based at the Villa Empain in Brussels.
boghossian.money: The Boghossian family of jewellers who created it.
boghossian.arts: In its first fifteen years it worked mainly on the living conditions of young people in Armenia and Lebanon.

bonnierfamilyfoundermoney.name: Bonnier AB
bonnierfamilyfoundermoney.what: A privately held Swedish group founded in 1804 by Gerhard Bonnier and controlled by the Bonnier family, with 175 companies in 15 countries.
bonnierfamilyfoundermoney.money: Media, real estate through Bonnier Fastigheter and investments through Bonnier Capital: EBITA of SEK 2,402 million in 2025.
bonnierfamilyfoundermoney.wrong_match: Konsthall C, a separate gallery in a former laundromat in Hökarängen, carries the Bonniers Konsthall sentence word for word.

britishcouncil|UK.name: British Council
britishcouncil|UK.what: The UK's cultural relations organisation under royal charter, a public corporation and charity sponsored by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.
britishcouncil|UK.money: Commercial income, 69 per cent of it from English teaching and exams in 2024-25, plus FCDO grant-in-aid of about 15 per cent.

brown.name: The Brown Foundation, Inc.
brown.what: A Houston family foundation set up in 1951 by the brothers Herman and George R. Brown and their wives, Margarett Root Brown and Alice Pratt Brown.
brown.money: The Brown brothers' fortune from Brown & Root, the construction firm merged with Halliburton in 1962.
brown.arts: It has distributed more than US$2 billion since 1951, with arts and education among its five areas.

bukhman.name: Bukhman Foundation
bukhman.what: A London charity (no. 1205571) set up in 2023 by Igor and Anastasia Bukhman; Igor co-founded the mobile games company Playrix with his brother Dmitry in 2004.
bukhman.money: Donations, £2.55 million of £2.57 million income in the year to March 2025; Igor Bukhman's fortune comes from Playrix.

bulgari.name: Bulgari S.p.A.
bulgari.what: An Italian luxury house founded in Rome in 1884 by the silversmith Sotirios Voulgaris, owned by the French group LVMH since 2011.
bulgari.money: Sales of jewellery, watches, fragrances, accessories and leather goods, as part of LVMH.

busanmetropolitancity|South Korea.name: Busan Metropolitan City
busanmetropolitancity|South Korea.what: The city government of Busan, South Korea's second most populous city, led by Mayor Jeon Jae-soo.
busanmetropolitancity|South Korea.money: Local taxes (5.38 trillion won), national subsidies (7.79 trillion won) and allocation tax in its 19.35 trillion won budget proposed for 2027.

caloustegulbenkian.name: Fundação Calouste Gulbenkian
caloustegulbenkian.what: A Portuguese foundation set up in Lisbon on 18 July 1956 under the will of Calouste Sarkis Gulbenkian, an Armenian oil magnate; it has a UK Branch and Paris centre.
caloustegulbenkian.money: The endowment Gulbenkian left from his oil fortune; it owned the oil company Partex until selling it to a Thai company in 2019.
caloustegulbenkian.arts: It runs the Calouste Gulbenkian Museum in Lisbon, which holds Gulbenkian's art collection.

canadacouncilforarts|Canada.name: Canada Council for the Arts
canadacouncilforarts|Canada.what: Canada's public arts funder, a federal Crown corporation set up in 1957 that reports to Parliament through the Minister of Canadian Heritage; based in Ottawa.
canadacouncilforarts|Canada.money: Annual appropriations from the Parliament of Canada, plus income from its endowment, donations and bequests.
canadacouncilforarts|Canada.arts: It also runs the Canada Council Art Bank, which rents out its collection of contemporary Canadian art.
canadacouncilforarts|Canada.address: 150 Elgin St, 2nd floor, Ottawa, Ontario K2P 1L4

canadalife.name: The Canada Life Assurance Company
canadalife.what: A Canadian insurer founded in 1847 in Hamilton, combined in 2020 with Great-West Life and London Life, with its head office in Winnipeg.
canadalife.money: Its insurance and wealth business; it is wholly owned by Great-West Lifeco, about 72% owned by Power Financial Corporation.
canadalife.address: 100 Osborne Street North, Winnipeg, MB R3C 1V3

carter.name: Amon G. Carter Foundation
carter.what: A Texas private foundation incorporated in 1945 by Amon G. Carter, publisher of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram, and his wife Nenetta Burton Carter, based in Fort Worth.
carter.money: An endowment seeded in 1947 with $8,511,712 from the sale of the Carters' Wasson Field oil interests; net assets were $553,053,361 in 2024.
carter.arts: Its grants cover art and culture among other fields, and its charitable gifts passed $900 million by 31 December 2025.
carter.address: 201 Main Street, Suite 1945, Fort Worth, TX 76102

casinosaustria.name: Casinos Austria AG
casinosaustria.what: An Austrian casino company founded in 1967 and based in Vienna; the Czech group Allwyn is its main shareholder and the state holding ÖBAG holds 33.24%.
casinosaustria.money: Gambling: its casinos and Austrian lotteries business brought gross gaming revenue of €1.56 billion in 2025.

chugokubank.name: The Chugoku Bank, Ltd.
chugokubank.what: A regional bank founded in Okayama on 21 December 1930, a subsidiary since October 2022 of the holding company Chugin Financial Group.
chugokubank.money: Banking; Chugin Financial Group reported total assets of ¥10.76 trillion and deposits of ¥8.31 trillion for 2024.

citibank.name: Citigroup Inc.
citibank.what: An American bank holding company in New York, formed in 1998 by merging Citicorp, parent of Citibank (chartered 1812), with Travelers.
citibank.money: Banking and financial services; it is the third-largest US banking institution by assets.

citybridge|UK.name: Bridge House Estates
citybridge|UK.what: The working name of Bridge House Estates, a London charity established by royal charter in 1282 to maintain London Bridge; its sole trustee is the City of London Corporation.
citybridge|UK.money: Income from its property and investment endowment: £31.2 million of £42.6 million income in the year to March 2025.

cityofcopenhagen|Denmark.name: Københavns Kommune
cityofcopenhagen|Denmark.what: Denmark's most populous municipality, covering central Copenhagen, with 673,575 residents in March 2026.
cityofcopenhagen|Denmark.money: The municipal budget, which the parties at City Hall agree each year.
cityofcopenhagen|Denmark.arts: The 2027 budget agreement sets aside DKK 19.3 million over three years for a partnership programme for the city's cultural life.

cityofdallas|USA.name: City of Dallas
cityofdallas|USA.what: The municipal government of Dallas, Texas, run under a council-manager system with a 14-member city council.
cityofdallas|USA.money: Property taxes and other city revenue: a FY 2025-26 budget of US$5.20 billion, of which the General Fund is US$1.9 billion.

cityofdenver|USA.name: City and County of Denver
cityofdenver|USA.what: The consolidated city and county government of Denver, Colorado, with an elected mayor and a 13-member city council.
cityofdenver|USA.money: Its General Fund, led by sales tax revenue, projected at US$1.68 billion for 2027.

cityofdsseldorf|Germany.name: Landeshauptstadt Düsseldorf
cityofdsseldorf|Germany.what: The municipal government of Düsseldorf, capital of the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia.
cityofdsseldorf|Germany.arts: Its Kulturamt gives grants for visual art, literature, music, performing arts and cultural education, and awards the city's Förderpreise.

cityofgeneva|Switzerland.name: Ville de Genève
cityofgeneva|Switzerland.what: The municipal government of Geneva, Switzerland, with a five-member Conseil administratif as executive and an elected Conseil municipal as assembly.
cityofgeneva|Switzerland.money: The city budget voted by the Conseil municipal: CHF 1.4 billion of spending and a CHF 69.9 million deficit for 2026.
cityofgeneva|Switzerland.address: Palais Eynard, Rue de la Croix-Rouge 4, 1204 Genève

cityofhelsinki|Finland.name: City of Helsinki
cityofhelsinki|Finland.what: The municipal government of Helsinki, Finland's capital, led by an 85-seat City Council; it is the only Finnish municipality that runs social, health and rescue services.
cityofhelsinki|Finland.money: Municipal income and property taxes; central government funds its social, health and rescue division. Municipal operating revenue was €1,383 million in 2025.

cityofparis|France.name: Ville de Paris
cityofparis|France.what: The municipal government of Paris, run by the Council of Paris and its Mayor, with the powers of both a commune and a département.
cityofparis|France.money: The City of Paris budget voted by the Council of Paris, which pays for culture mainly from operating spending.

cityofreykjavk|Iceland.name: Reykjavíkurborg
cityofreykjavk|Iceland.what: The municipal government of Reykjavík, Iceland's capital, run by a 23-member City Council elected for four-year terms.
cityofreykjavk|Iceland.money: The city budget set by the City Council; the 2025 budget, approved on 3 December 2024, planned a surplus of nearly ISK 1.3 billion.

cityofsanfrancisco|USA.name: City and County of San Francisco
cityofsanfrancisco|USA.what: The only consolidated city-county in California, governed by a strong mayor and the Board of Supervisors.
cityofsanfrancisco|USA.money: The city and county budget, about US$15.9 billion in fiscal 2024-25.

cityofstockholm|Sweden.name: Stockholms stad
cityofstockholm|Sweden.what: The municipal government of Stockholm, Sweden's most populous municipality, run by a 101-member municipal assembly elected every four years.
cityofstockholm|Sweden.money: The city budget adopted by the municipal assembly.

cityofvancouver|Canada.name: City of Vancouver
cityofvancouver|Canada.what: The municipal government of Vancouver, British Columbia, run by an elected mayor and ten councillors who serve four-year terms.
cityofvancouver|Canada.money: The City of Vancouver's municipal budget, which its elected council controls.

claralionel.name: Clara Lionel Foundation
claralionel.what: A US nonprofit founded in 2012 by the Barbadian singer Rihanna (Robyn Rihanna Fenty) and named after her grandparents Clara and Lionel Braithwaite, based in New York.
claralionel.money: Donations: contributions of US$21.4 million made up 89.1 percent of its 2024 revenue, and Fenty Beauty passes on 35 percent of selected sales.
claralionel.arts: Arts and culture is one of its five pillars. With the Mellon Foundation it runs The Ripple Effect, which supports artist-led projects from Barbados.

compagniadisanpaolo.name: Fondazione Compagnia di San Paolo
compagniadisanpaolo.what: A Turin philanthropic foundation that dates its work to 1563 and was the owner of the San Paolo bank, a forerunner of Intesa Sanpaolo.
compagniadisanpaolo.money: Returns on its invested assets, including a 6.627 per cent stake in Intesa Sanpaolo, Italy's largest bank (Consob, 27 October 2025).

conseildesartsdemontral.name: Conseil des arts de Montréal
conseildesartsdemontral.what: The arts council of the Urban Agglomeration of Montréal, active since 1956, which gives grants to Montréal artists, collectives and arts organisations.
conseildesartsdemontral.money: A yearly contribution from the agglomeration's budget: C$21,936,700 in 2025, frozen at the 2024 amount.
conseildesartsdemontral.arts: It invested C$19,528,703 in support programmes in 2025 and supported 763 organisations and collectives.
conseildesartsdemontral.address: 1210 Sherbrooke Street East, Montréal, QC H2L 1L9

creatensw.name: Create NSW
creatensw.what: The NSW Government's arts and culture agency, formed on 1 April 2017 from Arts NSW and Screen NSW.
creatensw.money: The New South Wales state budget, through the Minister for the Arts, who answers to the NSW Parliament.
creatensw.arts: Its Arts and Cultural Funding Program includes Creative Steps grants of up to $75,000 for new work by NSW artists.

creativeaustralia.name: Creative Australia
creativeaustralia.what: The Australian Government's principal arts investment and advisory body, founded as the Australia Council for the Arts in 1968 and renamed in 2023; based in Sydney.
creativeaustralia.money: The Australian Government, with funding decisions made at arm's length from the federal arts minister.

creativeindustriesnl.name: Stimuleringsfonds Creatieve Industrie
creativeindustriesnl.what: The Dutch national culture fund for design, architecture and digital culture, a private-law foundation and independent administrative body active since 1 January 2013, based in Rotterdam.
creativeindustriesnl.money: State money from the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science, the parent ministry of the national culture funds (rijkscultuurfondsen).

creativenewzealand.name: Arts Council of New Zealand Toi Aotearoa
creativenewzealand.what: The national arts development agency of the New Zealand government, a Crown entity governed by the Arts Council, set up in 1994 to replace the Queen Elizabeth II Arts Council.
creativenewzealand.money: The New Zealand Lottery Grants Board Te Puna Tahua and the government through Vote: Arts, Culture and Heritage.
creativenewzealand.arts: It invested NZ$61 million in the arts in 2024/25.

creativescotland.name: Creative Scotland
creativescotland.what: The Scottish Government's public body for the arts, screen and creative industries, created in 2010 from the Scottish Arts Council and Scottish Screen; based in Edinburgh.
creativescotland.money: Funding from the Scottish Government and the National Lottery.
creativescotland.address: Waverley Court, 4 East Market Street, Edinburgh EH8 8BG

creativevictoria.name: Creative Victoria
creativevictoria.what: The Victorian state government's agency for the arts and creative industries, reporting to the Minister for Creative Industries; based in Melbourne.
creativevictoria.money: The budget of the State of Victoria.

cultuurfonds.name: Cultuurfonds
cultuurfonds.what: A Dutch private foundation set up by Prince Bernhard in London in 1940, renamed in 2023 to drop his name, with its office in Amsterdam.
cultuurfonds.money: Proceeds from the VriendenLoterij and the Nederlandse Loterij, plus gifts and bequests from donors.
cultuurfonds.arts: It puts more than EUR 50 million a year into culture and nature.

deutschedenkmalschutz.name: Deutsche Stiftung Denkmalschutz
deutschedenkmalschutz.what: A privately funded foundation set up on 17 April 1985, the largest private initiative for monument preservation in Germany, with its seat in Bonn.
deutschedenkmalschutz.money: Gifts from about 200,000 private donors and money from the GlücksSpirale lottery.
deutschedenkmalschutz.arts: It has helped preserve more than 7,400 monuments with almost 800 million euros in funding.

doen.name: Stichting DOEN
doen.what: A Dutch foundation set up in 1991 by the Postcode Loterij that funds pioneers in the Netherlands and abroad.
doen.money: Lottery proceeds: 24,303,520 euros from the Postcode Loterij and 7,200,000 euros from the VriendenLoterij in 2025.
doen.arts: Its VriendenLoterij Fonds funded 70 art and culture projects in 2025.

dorotheum.name: Dorotheum
dorotheum.what: An auction house founded in Vienna in 1707 by Emperor Joseph I; a state enterprise until its 2001 sale to Erwin and Hanno Soravia and Christoph Dichand.
dorotheum.money: Its auctions, retail sales and pawn lending; about 600 auctions a year bring some 60 percent of its turnover.

dpartementdesbouchesdurhne.name: Département des Bouches-du-Rhône
dpartementdesbouchesdurhne.what: The departmental government of Bouches-du-Rhône in southern France, run by an elected departmental council presided over by Martine Vassal, seated in Marseille.
dpartementdesbouchesdurhne.money: The departmental budget its councillors adopted on 14 April 2026, with more than 1.6 billion euros, over 62 percent of spending, for social welfare.

droomendaad.name: Stichting Droom en Daad
droomendaad.what: A family foundation set up in Rotterdam on 13 December 2016 by Martijn van der Vorm, former chief executive of the investment company HAL; Van der Vorms chair its board.
droomendaad.money: The Van der Vorm family fortune, invested in HAL since the family sold its Holland America cruise business in 1988.
droomendaad.arts: It takes no applications and develops its own Rotterdam projects through foundations it sets up, among them the Fenix museum.

dubaiculture.name: Dubai Culture & Arts Authority
dubaiculture.what: A public authority of the Government of Dubai created by Law No. 6 of 2008, chaired since 5 September 2019 by Sheikha Latifa bint Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum.
dubaiculture.money: The general budget of the Emirate of Dubai, plus its own fees and grants or gifts approved by the Executive Council.

dublincitycouncil|Ireland.name: Dublin City Council
dublincitycouncil|Ireland.what: The local authority for the city of Dublin, called Dublin Corporation until 2001, with 63 elected members and a Lord Mayor.
dublincitycouncil|Ireland.money: The council's own budget, from which its Arts Office pays annual arts grants and bursary awards.
dublincitycouncil|Ireland.arts: It added €50,000 to its 2026 project grants and bursary awards.
dublincitycouncil|Ireland.address: Civic Offices, Wood Quay, Dublin 8, D08 RF3F

duvel.name: Duvel Moortgat
duvel.what: A Belgian family-owned brewer founded in 1871 by Jan-Leonard Moortgat, now in its fourth generation, based in Breendonk, Puurs-Sint-Amands.
duvel.money: Beer sales from brands including Duvel, Vedett, Chouffe and Liefmans: consolidated turnover of 608 million euros in 2024.

egdholding.name: EGD Holding AS
egdholding.what: A Bergen family investment company founded in 1907 by Einar Galtung Døsvig. Its chairman, Espen Galtung Døsvig, represents the fourth generation.
egdholding.money: The family's holdings in shipping (eight ships through EGD Shipholding), property (EGD Property) and financial investments (EGD Capital).
egdholding.arts: Its registered purpose includes buying and selling art and building and lending out an art collection.

enabel.name: Enabel
enabel.what: The Belgian federal government's agency for international cooperation, formerly the Belgian Technical Cooperation (CTB), with over 2,500 staff running over 200 projects.
enabel.money: Project work worth 500 million euros a year, at least half paid by the Belgian state, the rest by clients such as the European Union.

erste.name: DIE ERSTE österreichische Spar-Casse Privatstiftung
erste.what: Austria's largest savings bank foundation, formed in 2003 from Erste österreichische Spar-Casse, the first Austrian savings bank (1819), seated in Vienna.
erste.money: Dividends from its stake as core shareholder of Erste Group Bank AG, part of which it spends on Central and South Eastern Europe.

esmefairbairn.name: Esmée Fairbairn Foundation
esmefairbairn.what: An independent UK grant-making charity founded in 1961 by unit-trust pioneer Ian Fairbairn and named after his late second wife; based in London.
esmefairbairn.money: Investment returns on an endowment that began as a 33% stake in fund manager M&G, sold to Prudential in 1999.
esmefairbairn.arts: In 2025 it gave £52.9m across its three aims, one of which is Creative, Confident Communities.

estrelladamm.name: Sociedad Anónima Damm
estrelladamm.what: A Barcelona brewery founded in 1876 by the Alsatians August Kuentzmann Damm and Joseph Damm, maker of Estrella Damm beer.
estrelladamm.money: Beer and drinks sales, EUR 2,061 million in 2023; in 2018 the Carceller family held the largest stake through Disa, a Canarian oil company.

europeanregionaldevelopment.name: European Regional Development Fund
europeanregionaldevelopment.what: An EU fund set up in 1975 and one of the European Structural and Investment Funds, run by the European Commission's Directorate-General for Regional and Urban Policy.
europeanregionaldevelopment.money: The EU budget, spent through programmes shared between the Commission and national and regional authorities, which choose the projects.

federalgovernmentcommissionerforculture|.name: Der Beauftragte der Bundesregierung für Kultur und Medien
federalgovernmentcommissionerforculture|.short: Federal Government Commissioner for Culture and the Media (BKM)
federalgovernmentcommissionerforculture|.what: The German federal government's office for culture and media policy, headed by a Minister of State, currently Wolfram Weimer, with staff in Bonn and Berlin.
federalgovernmentcommissionerforculture|.money: The federal budget: the cabinet set about €2.5 billion for culture and media in 2026.

finnmarkcounty|Norway.name: Finnmark fylkeskommune
finnmarkcounty|Norway.what: The regional government of Finnmark county in northern Norway, re-established on 1 January 2024 after four years merged into Troms og Finnmark, with its administration in Vadsø.
finnmarkcounty|Norway.money: The county budget set by its elected county council.
finnmarkcounty|Norway.arts: It runs a culture and cultural heritage service and gives grants to festivals in the county.

flemishgovernment|Belgium.name: Vlaamse Regering
flemishgovernment|Belgium.what: The executive of the Flemish Community and Flemish Region of Belgium, led by a Minister-President and answerable to the Flemish Parliament.
flemishgovernment|Belgium.money: The Flemish public budget, which its Department of Culture, Youth and Media spends on arts subsidies under the Arts Decree (Kunstendecreet).

florahewlett.name: William and Flora Hewlett Foundation
florahewlett.what: A US private foundation in Menlo Park, California, set up in 1966 by Hewlett-Packard co-founder Bill Hewlett and his wife Flora.
florahewlett.money: An endowment of about US$13.9 billion at the end of 2024, from the Hewletts' personal gifts; it is independent of HP.
florahewlett.arts: Its Performing Arts programme awarded US$40.5 million in 94 grants in the San Francisco Bay Area in 2024.

fondazionecariplo.name: Fondazione Cariplo
fondazionecariplo.what: A foundation of banking origin created in Milan in December 1991, when the Amato law split the Cariplo savings bank into this foundation and a commercial bank.
fondazionecariplo.money: Returns on an endowment of 8,207,623,005 euros (2023) built on its stake in the Cariplo bank, which later merged into Intesa Sanpaolo.

fondazionecrfirenze.name: Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio di Firenze
fondazionecrfirenze.what: A Florence foundation of banking origin, created in April 1992 when the Cassa di Risparmio di Firenze, a savings bank founded by 100 citizens in 1829, became a company.
fondazionecrfirenze.money: Returns on an endowment of about 2 billion euros inherited from the savings bank, including a holding in Intesa Sanpaolo.
fondazionecrfirenze.arts: Culture is one of its four missions, and its endowment includes an art collection.

fondazionecrt.name: Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio di Torino
fondazionecrt.what: A banking foundation formed in Turin in 1991, when the Cassa di Risparmio di Torino moved its banking business into a separate company; Italy's third-largest by assets.
fondazionecrt.money: Returns on its endowment, inherited from the Cassa di Risparmio di Torino and long including a large UniCredit shareholding.
fondazionecrt.arts: It has given more than 2 billion euros to over 50,000 projects in art, research, training, welfare, environment and innovation.

forartsinitiatives.name: Foundation for Arts Initiatives
forartsinitiatives.what: A New York grant-making foundation that began in 1931 as the American Center for Students and Artists in Paris and took its present name in 2008.
forartsinitiatives.money: An endowment created from the 1996 sale of the American Center's Paris building to the French Ministry of Culture, now about $30 million.
forartsinitiatives.arts: It has made more than 800 grants totalling nearly $20 million to artists, curators and independent art spaces in many countries.

foyle.name: The Foyle Foundation
foyle.what: A UK grant-making charity formed in 2000 to carry out the will of bookseller Christina Foyle; it closed in December 2025 and entered voluntary liquidation in June 2026.
foyle.money: The estate of Christina Foyle, daughter of a founder of Foyles bookshop on Charing Cross Road, London.
foyle.arts: From 2000 to 2025 it gave over £185M to almost 7,500 charities and state schools, mainly for arts and learning.

frankenthaler.name: Helen Frankenthaler Foundation, Inc.
frankenthaler.what: A New York non-profit formed by the painter Helen Frankenthaler in 1984; it became active in 2013, when her estate closed.
frankenthaler.money: Endowed by the artist; net assets were $173,182,625 in 2024, when sales of assets brought 86.3% of revenue.
frankenthaler.arts: Its Frankenthaler Climate Initiative made its first grants, totalling $5.1 million, in July 2021.

freelands.name: Freelands Foundation
freelands.what: A London art education charity set up in 2015 by the media executive Elisabeth Murdoch, who chairs its board.
freelands.money: Investment income on a large 2019 donation, plus services donated by Freelands Group, owned by a trust of which Elisabeth Murdoch is a beneficiary.
freelands.arts: In 2025 it paid grants totalling £1,475,492 to 28 organisations.

frenchstate|France.name: Ministère de la Culture
frenchstate|France.what: The culture ministry of the French state, set up in 1959 with André Malraux as minister; its regional directorates of cultural affairs (DRAC) fund institutions across France.
frenchstate|France.money: The French state budget: the 2026 finance bill requested €3.747 billion in payment credits for the Culture mission.
frenchstate|France.renamed: Same body as the atlas entry ministredelaculture; the DRAC named in two sentences are the ministry's regional offices.

fukutake.name: Fukutake Foundation
fukutake.what: A Japanese foundation that runs Benesse Art Site Naoshima with Benesse Corporation, grown from a foundation Soichiro Fukutake set up in 2004.
fukutake.money: A personal endowment from Soichiro Fukutake, former head of Benesse, the Okayama correspondence education and publishing company.
fukutake.arts: It has been a founding patron of CIMAM, the international committee for modern art museums, since 2000.

fundacilacaixa.name: Fundación "la Caixa"
fundacilacaixa.what: A Spanish banking foundation that grew out of the la Caixa savings bank, headquartered in Barcelona since March 2025.
fundacilacaixa.money: Dividends from its holding company CriteriaCaixa, which holds 31 per cent of CaixaBank and 9.99 per cent of Telefónica.
fundacilacaixa.arts: Its social work budget, which covers cultural as well as social and scientific projects, is €710 million for 2026.

fundacinbbva.name: Fundación BBVA
fundacinbbva.what: The foundation of the Spanish banking group BBVA, with headquarters in Bilbao and an office in Madrid.
fundacinbbva.money: The BBVA Group, whose corporate social responsibility the foundation carries out.

fundacinmutuamadrilea.name: Fundación Mutua Madrileña
fundacinmutuamadrilea.what: The foundation of the Spanish insurer Mutua Madrileña, set up in 2003 for medical research and widened to social, road safety and cultural work in 2009.
fundacinmutuamadrilea.money: Funds from Mutua Madrileña, the Madrid insurer founded in 1930 that sells car, health and life insurance.
fundacinmutuamadrilea.arts: Cultural work takes about a quarter of the foundation's resources (2024).

germanysforeignoffice.name: Auswärtiges Amt
germanysforeignoffice.what: Germany's federal foreign ministry, based in Berlin with a second seat in Bonn; it runs the foreign service and German foreign and European policy.
germanysforeignoffice.money: The German federal budget, as a supreme federal authority.

goetheinstitut.name: Goethe-Institut e.V.
goetheinstitut.what: Germany's cultural institute, a registered association headquartered in Munich with more than 150 centres in 99 countries that teach German and run cultural exchange.
goetheinstitut.money: Mainly annual grants from the German Federal Foreign Office, plus its own tuition and exam fees and money from sponsors and patrons.

goldshoman.name: Abdul Hameed Shoman Foundation
goldshoman.what: A non-profit foundation that Arab Bank set up in Amman in 1978 to support science, the humanities and culture in the Arab world.
goldshoman.money: Arab Bank's profits: in 2011 the bank gave it over 8 million Jordanian dinars, about 87% of its community investment budget.
goldshoman.arts: It runs a cultural forum, film screenings and musical evenings in Amman, and gives cultural grants and an award for creativity.

goldsmith.name: Horace W. Goldsmith Foundation
goldsmith.what: A New York private foundation created in 1955 by Horace Ward Goldsmith, who bought a New York Stock Exchange seat in 1927.
goldsmith.money: Investment returns, chiefly gains on asset sales and dividends, on assets of $826 million in 2024.

gucci.name: Guccio Gucci S.p.A.
gucci.what: An Italian luxury fashion house founded in Florence in 1921 by Guccio Gucci and owned since 1999 by the French luxury group Kering.
gucci.money: Sales of clothing, leather goods, shoes and accessories: 7.65 billion euros in 2024.

gulbenkian.name: Fundação Calouste Gulbenkian
gulbenkian.what: A Portuguese foundation set up in Lisbon in 1956 under the will of Calouste Gulbenkian, an Armenian oil magnate; it runs the Gulbenkian Museum and Orchestra.
gulbenkian.money: An endowment from Calouste Gulbenkian's oil fortune; it fully owned the oil company Partex until selling it to a Thai company in 2019.

hauser.name: Hauser & Wirth
hauser.what: A commercial art gallery founded in Zurich in 1992 by Iwan Wirth, Manuela Wirth and Ursula Hauser, with galleries in Europe, Asia and North America.
hauser.money: Its gallery business: it represents over 80 artists and estates, including those of Philip Guston and Louise Bourgeois.

helis.name: The Helis Foundation
helis.what: A Louisiana private foundation established and funded in 1955 by the family of William Helis, a Greek emigrant to New Orleans who made a fortune in oil.
helis.money: The Helis family's oil fortune, plus art funds bequeathed by Diana Helis Henry and Adrienne Helis Malvin. Total assets were US$82,984,093 in 2024.
helis.arts: Its Art Funds paid for Prospect.3's Basquiat and the Bayou and for installing Lynda Benglis's The Wave of the World in New Orleans City Park.
helis.address: 201 St. Charles Avenue, Suite 2600, New Orleans, LA

henrymoore.name: The Henry Moore Foundation
henrymoore.what: A charity founded in 1977 by sculptor Henry Moore and his family, with headquarters at his former home in Perry Green, Hertfordshire, and the Henry Moore Institute in Leeds.
henrymoore.money: A founding gift from Henry Moore and his family; it also administers the sale and exhibition of Moore's work.
henrymoore.arts: Henry Moore Grants fund sculpture exhibitions, commissions, acquisitions and research, with grants of up to £20,000 in the main categories.
henrymoore.address: Dane Tree House, Perry Green, Much Hadham SG10 6EE

hiscox.name: Hiscox Ltd
hiscox.what: An insurance group listed on the London Stock Exchange and based in Hamilton, Bermuda, grown from a Lloyd's of London underwriting agency that began in 1901.
hiscox.money: Specialist insurance, including property, casualty, kidnap and ransom and hacking cover: revenue of £4,883.7 million in 2025.

hugoboss.name: HUGO BOSS AG
hugoboss.what: A German fashion company founded in 1924 by Hugo Ferdinand Boss in Metzingen, majority-owned since October 2026 by the British retailer Frasers Group.
hugoboss.money: Sales of BOSS and HUGO clothing, shoes and accessories: 4.27 billion euros in 2025.
hugoboss.arts: It has funded the HUGO BOSS PRIZE with the Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation since 1996 and gave the HUGO BOSS ASIA ART Award from 2013.

hyundai.name: Hyundai Motor Company
hyundai.what: A South Korean carmaker established in 1967 and based in Seoul, which owns the Genesis brand and 33.88 per cent of Kia.
hyundai.money: Car sales: revenue of KRW 186.3 trillion and net profit of KRW 10.36 trillion in 2025.
hyundai.arts: Its Hyundai Artlab team runs long-term partnerships with Tate, LACMA, the Whitney Museum and the Korean Pavilion at the Venice Biennale.

imls.name: Institute of Museum and Library Services
imls.what: An independent US federal agency established in 1996 by the Museum and Library Services Act; the main source of federal support for US libraries and museums.
imls.arts: In 2024 it awarded $266.7 million through grantmaking, research and policy work.

institutfranais.name: Institut français
institutfranais.what: France's public agency for cultural diplomacy, a state industrial and commercial body set up in 2011 under the foreign and culture ministries; seated in Paris.
institutfranais.money: The French state budget, through the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Culture.
institutfranais.arts: It supports French artists and creative industries abroad and coordinates France's cultural network of more than 150 branches.

ireneludwig.name: Peter und Irene Ludwig Stiftung
ireneludwig.what: A charitable foundation under German civil law, set up in Aachen in 1997 by Irene Ludwig from the foundation she and Peter Ludwig had founded in 1982.
ireneludwig.money: The art collection and fortune of Peter and Irene Ludwig; Peter Ludwig built up the chocolate maker Leonard Monheim, later Ludwig Schokolade.
ireneludwig.arts: It buys, manages and lends works for the Ludwig museums and supports exhibitions; a 2017 contract with the City of Cologne covers its work with Museum Ludwig.
ireneludwig.renamed: The Cologne, Beijing and Havana sentences describe gifts by Peter and Irene Ludwig themselves; the 1976 Museum Ludwig gift came before the foundation existed.

jameelfamily.name: Abdul Latif Jameel Company Ltd
jameelfamily.what: A family-owned diversified business founded in Jeddah in 1945 by Sheikh Abdul Latif Jameel, active in more than 30 countries.
jameelfamily.money: Its businesses in vehicle distribution, as a Toyota distributor in Saudi Arabia since 1955, and in finance, machinery, real estate, energy and consumer products.
jameelfamily.arts: Through Art Jameel, which the family founded in 2003 and funds privately, it supports the Jameel Arts Centre in Dubai, a free contemporary art institution.

janetbuxton.name: Michael and Janet Buxton Foundation
janetbuxton.what: The philanthropic foundation of the Melbourne art collectors Michael and Janet Buxton, through which they founded Buxton Contemporary at the University of Melbourne.
janetbuxton.money: The Buxtons' own wealth. Michael Buxton co-founded the Melbourne property developer MAB Corporation with Andrew Buxton in 1995.
janetbuxton.arts: In 2014 it gave the university their collection of contemporary Australian art and funds to build the gallery, which opened in 2018.
janetbuxton.renamed: The museum sentences mean Michael and Janet Buxton and their foundation, not MAB Corporation, the property company Michael Buxton co-founded.

japan.name: The Japan Foundation
japan.what: A Japanese public body for international cultural exchange, set up in 1972 by an Act of the Diet, an Independent Administrative Institution since 2003.
japan.money: The Japanese state, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which oversees it.

japansagencyforculturalaffairs|Japan.name: Agency for Cultural Affairs, Government of Japan
japansagencyforculturalaffairs|Japan.what: A special body of Japan's Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology, set up in 1968 to promote arts and culture, with its main offices in Kyoto since 2023.
japansagencyforculturalaffairs|Japan.money: Japan's national budget through the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology; its budget was 107 billion yen in 2026.
japansagencyforculturalaffairs|Japan.arts: Its divisions protect the nation's cultural properties and oversee the Japan Arts Council.

japantobacco.name: Japan Tobacco Inc.
japantobacco.what: A Japanese tobacco company set up in 1985 to take over the state tobacco monopoly and parent of Japan Tobacco International. By law the government owns at least one third.
japantobacco.money: Tobacco sales, which drove most of its growth: revenue of 3.47 trillion yen in 2025, up 13.4 percent.

jpmorgan.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
jpmorgan.what: The largest US bank, formed in 2000 by the merger of J.P. Morgan & Co. and Chase Manhattan, headquartered at 270 Park Avenue, New York.
jpmorgan.money: Interest and fees from consumer, commercial and investment banking: net income was $57.0 billion in 2025.

kpmg.name: KPMG Argentina
kpmg.what: The Argentine member firm of KPMG, the London-based Big Four network of audit, tax and advisory firms, with its Buenos Aires office at Bouchard 710.
kpmg.money: Fees for audit, tax and advisory work paid by its clients.
kpmg.wrong_match: The Kunstmuseum Basel and Kunstsammlung Nordrhein-Westfalen sentences mean KPMG's Swiss and German member firms, which are separate firms in the same network.

kulturstiftungdesbundes.name: Kulturstiftung des Bundes
kulturstiftungdesbundes.what: An independent foundation set up in 2002 with seat in Halle an der Saale that funds contemporary art and culture across Germany and abroad.
kulturstiftungdesbundes.money: German federal funds: an annual budget of 35 million euros.
kulturstiftungdesbundes.arts: Since 2002 it has run over 40 funding programmes and backed about 4,000 projects, with multi-year support for documenta and the Berliner Theatertreffen.

kunststiftungnrw.name: Kunststiftung NRW
kunststiftungnrw.what: A public-law foundation set up on 12 September 1989 by the North Rhine-Westphalia state government under Johannes Rau, based in the Haus der Stiftungen in Düsseldorf.
kunststiftungnrw.money: The proceeds of the lottery operator WestLotto.
kunststiftungnrw.arts: It has funded about 12,000 projects in literature, music, performing arts and visual art with a link to North Rhine-Westphalia since 1989.

lambent.name: Lambent Foundation
lambent.what: A New York grantmaker for art, culture and social justice founded by the artist Anne Delaney, grown out of her Starry Night Fund of 2002.
lambent.money: Anne Delaney's philanthropy, held as a fiscally sponsored project of the Tides Center, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit.

lambent.address: 55 Exchange Place, Suite 406, New York, NY 10005

landvorarlberg|Austria.name: Amt der Vorarlberger Landesregierung
landvorarlberg|Austria.what: The administration of the government of the Austrian state of Vorarlberg, population 401,674, led by Landeshauptmann Markus Wallner (ÖVP) and seated in the Landhaus in Bregenz.
landvorarlberg|Austria.money: The state budget of Vorarlberg, which plans €2.8 billion in spending for 2026, including about €200 million in new borrowing.

lazraqfamily.name: Alliances Développement Immobilier
lazraqfamily.what: A Moroccan property developer listed in Casablanca, founded by Alami Lazraq, who chairs it and controls 51.7 percent of its shares.
lazraqfamily.money: Sales of residential, commercial and tourism property developments across North Africa.
lazraqfamily.arts: Its cultural patronage covers the Fondation MACAAL, built on the art collection of Alami and Farida Lazraq, and a sculpture park.

leventis.name: A. G. Leventis Foundation
leventis.what: A private foundation set up in May 1979 under provisions made by Anastasios G. Leventis, a Greek Cypriot trader in West Africa, with its executive office in Zurich.
leventis.money: The fortune Anastasios G. Leventis made with A. G. Leventis & Company, his West African trading group founded in 1936.
leventis.arts: Its own initiatives are the A. G. Leventis Gallery and the Leventis Municipal Museum, and it gives grants for heritage conservation, museums and libraries.

linbury.name: The Linbury Trust
linbury.what: A UK grant-making trust, one of the Sainsbury Family Charitable Trusts, set up by Lord Sainsbury of Preston Candover and the ballerina Anya Linden, first granting in 1973.
linbury.money: Investment income and donations; it held funds of £135.0 million at 5 April 2025.
linbury.arts: In the year to April 2025 it paid £3.7 million to culture, including £2.25 million to the National Gallery's Sainsbury Wing.
linbury.address: The Peak, 5 Wilton Road, London SW1V 1AP

liverpoolcitycouncil|UK.name: Liverpool City Council
liverpoolcitycouncil|UK.what: The local authority for the city of Liverpool, a metropolitan borough council since 1974, under Labour control since 2010, with main offices in the Cunard Building.
liverpoolcitycouncil|UK.money: Business rates (£295.1m), council tax (£277.0m) and general government grants (£245.5m) in its 2026-27 budget, £1.8bn gross.

loterieromande.name: Société de la loterie de la Suisse romande
loterieromande.what: A public-benefit lottery and sports betting company created in 1937 under an agreement between the governments of the French-speaking Swiss cantons, based in Lausanne; Jura joined in 1979.
loterieromande.money: Lottery and sports betting: gross gaming revenue was CHF 429.8 million in 2025, and its whole profit, CHF 252 million, went to associations.
loterieromande.arts: Its profit goes to associations in culture, social welfare, health, research, education, the environment, tourism, heritage and sport.

ludwig.name: Peter und Irene Ludwig Stiftung
ludwig.what: A foundation in Aachen set up in 1997 by Irene Ludwig, a year after the death of her husband Peter Ludwig, to place their collection in public museums.
ludwig.money: The fortune of Irene and Peter Ludwig, who ran the Monheim chocolate company until its sale in 1986, then Ludwig Schokolade until 1998.

luma.name: LUMA Foundation
luma.what: A Zurich non-profit set up in 2004 by Maja Hoffmann to support contemporary artists; it created the LUMA Arles arts campus, launched in 2013.
luma.money: Its founder Maja Hoffmann belongs to the shareholder pool of Roche founder descendants, which controls Roche Holding.

manitobaartscouncil|Canada.name: Manitoba Arts Council
manitobaartscouncil|Canada.what: An arm's-length agency of the Province of Manitoba, established in 1965, that makes awards to professional artists and arts organisations through peer assessment.
manitobaartscouncil|Canada.money: The Manitoba provincial budget, through the department of Sport, Culture, Heritage and Tourism.
manitobaartscouncil|Canada.arts: Its budget was C$12.7 million in 2023.

massachusettsculturalcouncil|USA.name: Mass Cultural Council
massachusettsculturalcouncil|USA.what: The public arts funding body of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, based in Boston, which makes grants to cultural organizations, schools, communities and individual artists.
massachusettsculturalcouncil|USA.money: An annual appropriation from the Massachusetts Legislature, plus funds from the National Endowment for the Arts.
massachusettsculturalcouncil|USA.address: 10 St. James Avenue, 3rd Floor, Boston, MA 02116-3803

mazda.name: Mazda Motor Corporation
mazda.what: A Japanese carmaker founded on 30 January 1920 as Toyo Cork Kogyo by Jujiro Matsuda, headquartered in Fuchu, Hiroshima Prefecture.
mazda.money: Sales of cars and commercial vehicles: net sales of 4,918.2 billion yen in the year to March 2026.

michaelaudain.name: Michael Audain
michaelaudain.what: A Canadian home builder and art collector, born in 1937, chairman since 1992 and a major shareholder of Polygon Homes Ltd. in Vancouver.
michaelaudain.money: His stake in Polygon Homes; he gives mainly through the Audain Foundation, which he set up in 1997 with Yoshiko Karasawa.
michaelaudain.arts: The Audain Foundation funds the annual C$100,000 Audain Prize for the Visual Arts and gave C$2 million to Arts Umbrella in 2023.

ministredelaculture|France.name: Ministère de la Culture
ministredelaculture|France.what: France's culture ministry, created in 1959 by President Charles de Gaulle for André Malraux, with offices on the rue de Valois in Paris and regional offices (DRAC).
ministredelaculture|France.money: The French state budget: the 2026 finance bill requested €3.747 billion in payment credits for the Culture mission.

ministryofocw|Netherlands.name: Ministerie van Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap
ministryofocw|Netherlands.short: Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science (OCW)
ministryofocw|Netherlands.what: The Dutch national ministry for education, culture and science, created in 1918 and based in The Hague.
ministryofocw|Netherlands.money: The Dutch state budget, with €618 million a year in 2025-2028 for culture paid through the national cultural infrastructure and six national culture funds.

mllerfonden.name: A.P. Møller og Hustru Chastine Mc-Kinney Møllers Fond til almene Formaal
mllerfonden.what: A commercial foundation set up in Copenhagen in 1953 by the shipowner Arnold Peter Møller, split from a family foundation he had created in 1946.
mllerfonden.money: Its holdings through A.P. Moller Holding, its investment arm since 2013, which owns the majority of the Maersk shipping and logistics group.

mlleroghustruchastinemckinneymllersfond.name: A.P. Møller og Hustru Chastine Mc-Kinney Møllers Fond til almene Formaal
mlleroghustruchastinemckinneymllersfond.what: A commercial foundation set up in Copenhagen in 1953 by the shipowner Arnold Peter Møller, split from a family foundation he had created in 1946.
mlleroghustruchastinemckinneymllersfond.money: Its holdings through A.P. Moller Holding, its investment arm since 2013, which owns the majority of the Maersk shipping and logistics group.
mlleroghustruchastinemckinneymllersfond.arts: Its purposes include Danish culture and the upkeep of buildings of cultural and historical value; it paid to restore Kastellet in Copenhagen in 1989 and 1999.

mondriaan.name: Mondriaan Fonds
mondriaan.what: The Dutch public fund for visual art and cultural heritage, formed in Amsterdam in 2012 by merging the Mondriaan Stichting (set up 1994) with Fonds BKVB.
mondriaan.money: The Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science.
mondriaan.arts: In 2024 it approved 2,257 of 4,204 applications, awarding 53,438,678 euros in total.

morrison.name: Allies and Morrison LLP
morrison.what: A London architecture and urban planning practice founded in 1984 by Bob Allies and Graham Morrison, with studios in Cambridge, Manchester, Dublin, Jeddah and Toronto.
morrison.money: Fees from architecture, urban planning and consultancy commissions, much of it repeat work for long-term clients.

nationalendowmentforarts.name: National Endowment for the Arts
nationalendowmentforarts.what: An independent agency of the US federal government, created by Congress in 1965 and signed into law by President Lyndon B. Johnson; based in Washington, D.C.
nationalendowmentforarts.money: Annual appropriations from the US Congress: $207,000,000 a year for 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026.

nationallotteryheritage.name: The National Lottery Heritage Fund
nationallotteryheritage.what: The UK distributor of National Lottery money for heritage, set up in 1994 as the Heritage Lottery Fund and renamed in 2019; head office in London.
nationallotteryheritage.money: A share of National Lottery proceeds raised from players, plus heritage funding it distributes for the UK and devolved governments.
nationallotteryheritage.arts: Since 1994 it has awarded over £9.9 billion of National Lottery and other funding to more than 54,000 projects.
nationallotteryheritage.address: 4th Floor, Cannon Bridge House, 25 Dowgate Hill, London EC4R 2YA

nationallottery|Belgium.name: Loterie Nationale / Nationale Loterij
nationallottery|Belgium.what: Belgium's largest lottery operator, founded in 1934 as the Colonial Lottery and a public-law limited company since 2002, under the Federal Public Service Finance.
nationallottery|Belgium.money: Sales of its lottery games and Scooore sports betting; it pays a monopoly fee to the federal treasury.
nationallottery|Belgium.arts: Parliament decides which projects and organisations receive its yearly subsidies.

nationaltrustforhistoric.name: National Trust for Historic Preservation in the United States
nationaltrustforhistoric.what: A privately funded nonprofit founded in 1949 by congressional charter and based in Washington, D.C.; it runs historic sites and campaigns to save historic places.
nationaltrustforhistoric.money: Contributions, 66.1% of US$104.9 million revenue in the year to June 2025, plus investment income and asset sales.

newcarlsberg.name: Ny Carlsbergfondet
newcarlsberg.what: A private foundation for the arts set up by charter on 20 January 1902 by the brewer Carl Jacobsen and his wife Ottilia, based in Copenhagen.
newcarlsberg.money: Dividends from Carlsberg A/S shares, passed on by the Carlsberg Foundation under its charter, and returns on its other investments.
newcarlsberg.arts: It donates artworks to Danish museums, commissions site-specific art (decorative projects) and gives art awards.

newyorkstatecouncilonarts|USA.name: New York State Council on the Arts
newyorkstatecouncilonarts|USA.what: A New York State agency for the arts, established in 1960 through a bill in the State Legislature backed by Governor Nelson Rockefeller.
newyorkstatecouncilonarts|USA.money: The New York State budget, enacted by the Governor and Legislature.
newyorkstatecouncilonarts|USA.arts: Its grants reached $80.9 million in fiscal year 2026, and over $161 million including capital funding.

nordea.name: Nordea-fonden
nordea.what: A Danish commercial foundation set up in 1989 by the savings bank Sparekassen SDS when it became a limited company, named Nordea-fonden since 2008.
nordea.money: Returns on its assets, chiefly a stake of about 4.4 percent in Nordea Bank Abp. It gives over 80 percent of yearly returns to charity.
nordea.arts: Culture is one of its four areas of support, alongside health, exercise and nature, with a grant pool for culture houses (Kulturhuspuljen).
nordea.address: Heerings Gaard, Overgaden neden Vandet 11, 1414 Copenhagen K

nottinghamcitycouncil|UK.name: Nottingham City Council
nottinghamcitycouncil|UK.what: The unitary local authority for the city of Nottingham, under Labour control since 1991, with main offices at Loxley House.
nottinghamcitycouncil|UK.money: UK government grants, including the Revenue Support Grant, and council tax.

nrwcultureministry|Germany.name: Ministerium für Kultur und Wissenschaft des Landes Nordrhein-Westfalen
nrwcultureministry|Germany.what: The culture and science ministry of the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia in Düsseldorf, led by Minister Ina Brandes.
nrwcultureministry|Germany.arts: In June 2026 it granted about 18 million euros to Kultur Ruhr GmbH for the Ruhrtriennale, Chorwerk Ruhr, Tanzlandschaft Ruhr and Urbane Künste Ruhr.

nswgovernment|Australia.name: NSW Government
nswgovernment|Australia.what: The state government of New South Wales, Australia, led since March 2023 by the Labor Premier Chris Minns.
nswgovernment|Australia.money: The New South Wales state budget, which funds the arts through Create NSW and its Arts and Cultural Funding Program.
nswgovernment|Australia.renamed: The museum sentences mean the NSW Government as a whole, not its Premier's Department, the agency that leads the state public service.

nycarlsberg.name: Ny Carlsbergfondet
nycarlsberg.what: A Danish art foundation set up in 1902 by the brewer Carl Jacobsen and based in Copenhagen.
nycarlsberg.money: Dividends from shares in Carlsberg A/S, passed on by the Carlsberg Foundation under its charter, plus returns on its own investments.

nycarlsbergfondet.name: Ny Carlsbergfondet
nycarlsbergfondet.what: A Danish art foundation set up on 20 January 1902 by the brewer Carl Jacobsen and his wife Ottilia Jacobsen, operating under the Carlsberg Foundation in Copenhagen.
nycarlsbergfondet.money: Mainly dividends from shares in the brewer Carlsberg A/S.
nycarlsbergfondet.arts: It funds visual art, applied art and architecture in Denmark, including gifts of works to museums and decorative commissions.

nycculturalaffairs|USA.name: New York City Department of Cultural Affairs
nycculturalaffairs|USA.what: The New York City government department for culture, a separate city agency since 1976, headed by a commissioner the mayor appoints.
nycculturalaffairs|USA.money: The City of New York's budget.
nycculturalaffairs|USA.arts: Its programmes include Materials for the Arts, which collects donated materials and delivers them to its members.

nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs.name: New York City Department of Cultural Affairs
nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs.what: The New York City agency that funds non-profit culture in the five boroughs, a separate city agency since 1976.
nycdepartmentofculturalaffairs.money: New York City's budget: an operating budget of $300 million in fiscal 2026, almost entirely city money.
