nysca.name: New York State Council on the Arts
nysca.what: A New York State agency for the arts, established in 1960 through a bill in the State Legislature backed by Governor Nelson Rockefeller.
nysca.money: The New York State budget, enacted by the Governor and Legislature.
nysca.arts: Its grants reached $80.9 million in fiscal year 2026, and over $161 million including capital funding.

ocw.name: Ministerie van Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap
ocw.what: The Dutch national ministry for education, culture and science in The Hague, led in 2026 by Minister Rianne Letschert.
ocw.money: The Dutch national budget: 57 billion euros of spending set for 2026.
ocw.arts: Its 2026 budget sets 2.7 billion euros for culture and media.

okayamagas.name: Okayama Gas Co., Ltd.
okayamagas.what: A city gas company founded in Okayama on 29 January 1910, supplying Okayama, Kurashiki, Akaiwa, Tamano, Soja and Hayashima.
okayamagas.money: Sales of city gas, gas appliances and pipe work; non-consolidated revenue was ¥24.81 billion in 2015.

onassis.name: Alexander S. Onassis Public Benefit Foundation
onassis.what: A private foundation set up in Vaduz, Liechtenstein, in 1975 under the will of the shipowner Aristotle Onassis, in memory of his son Alexander.
onassis.money: Profits of the Onassis Business Foundation, its holding for maritime transport and real estate, formed from half of Aristotle Onassis's estate.
onassis.arts: It endows Greek studies chairs at universities and runs Onassis USA, its New York affiliate based in the Olympic Tower on Fifth Avenue.

ontarioartscouncil|Canada.name: Ontario Arts Council
ontarioartscouncil|Canada.what: An arm's-length agency of the Ontario government, created by provincial law in 1963 under Premier John Robarts; based in Toronto.
ontarioartscouncil|Canada.money: The Government of Ontario, through its culture ministry.
ontarioartscouncil|Canada.arts: It runs more than fifty funding programmes for Ontario artists and arts organisations.
ontarioartscouncil|Canada.address: 121 Bloor Street East, 7th Floor, Toronto, ON M4W 3M5

opensociety.name: Open Society Foundations
opensociety.what: A grantmaking network founded by investor George Soros, begun with a Budapest foundation in 1984; the Open Society Institute was set up in New York in 1993.
opensociety.money: George Soros's personal fortune: he had given over $32 billion by 2017, including an $18 billion transfer announced that year.

palmacouncil|Spain.name: Ajuntament de Palma
palmacouncil|Spain.what: The municipal government of Palma, Mallorca, a city of 438,234 people in 2024, led by mayor Jaime Martínez Llabrés of the People's Party.
palmacouncil|Spain.money: The city's municipal budget, set at €626.67 million for 2026 and approved by the council in December 2025.

partnersincludeafricanculture.name: African Culture Fund
partnersincludeafricanculture.what: A pan-African non-profit trust set up in Bamako in February 2018 by African artists and cultural actors, registered in Mali under a headquarters agreement.

partnersincludeafricanculture.arts: It finances artistic projects across Africa through calls for projects and trains cultural managers through its ACF Academy.

paulgettytrust.name: J. Paul Getty Trust
paulgettytrust.what: A trust founded in 1953 by J. Paul Getty, founder of Getty Oil, that runs the Getty Museum, Research Institute, Conservation Institute and Getty Foundation in Los Angeles.
paulgettytrust.money: An endowment of US$9.4 billion (2025) built on Getty's bequest, which included nearly $660 million in Getty Oil stock received in 1982.
paulgettytrust.arts: The Getty Foundation gives grants to museums and cultural institutions worldwide.

paulhamlyn.name: Paul Hamlyn Foundation
paulhamlyn.what: An independent UK grant-making charity started by publisher Paul Hamlyn in 1987 and in its current form since 2004; based in King's Cross, London.
paulhamlyn.money: An endowment from Paul Hamlyn's publishing fortune: a £50m gift in 1987 and about £308 million from his estate in 2001.
paulhamlyn.arts: It funds children and young people, with a focus on the arts.

pellerestates.name: Andrew Peller Limited
pellerestates.what: A Canadian wine producer listed in Toronto and based in Grimsby, Ontario, whose brands include Peller Estates; in June 2026 it agreed to be bought by Fairfax Financial.
pellerestates.money: Sales of wine, ciders and spirits, including through 101 company stores in Ontario; revenue was C$393.0 million in the year to 31 March 2026.

phillips.name: Phillips
phillips.what: An auction house founded in London in 1796, with head offices in London and New York and a UK holding company, Phillips Assets Ltd.
phillips.money: Fees on auction and private sales (UK turnover £89m in 2024), under a parent, Mercury Group Trading, controlled by Leonid Fridlyand and Leonid Strunin.

pnc.name: The PNC Financial Services Group, Inc.
pnc.what: A US bank holding company in Pittsburgh, tracing to the Pittsburgh Trust and Savings Company of 1845 and formed as PNC by a 1982 merger.
pnc.money: Interest and fees from personal, small business and corporate banking through PNC Bank; revenue was US$21.49 billion in 2023.

polygonhomes.name: Polygon Homes Ltd.
polygonhomes.what: A Metro Vancouver home builder in business since 1980, chaired by its major shareholder Michael Audain.
polygonhomes.money: Sales of the homes it builds and develops, more than 35,000 to date, from masterplanned communities to high-rise towers.
polygonhomes.address: Suite 900-1333 West Broadway, Vancouver, BC V6H 4C2

power.name: Power Corporation of Canada
power.what: A Canadian holding company founded in 1925 and based in Montreal, controlled since 1968 by a group led by Paul Desmarais.
power.money: Its financial services holdings in insurance, retirement, wealth and asset management, which have included Great-West Life, Canada Life, IGM Financial and Mackenzie.

princeclaus.name: Prince Claus Fund
princeclaus.what: A Dutch fund set up in 1996 and named after Prince Claus of the Netherlands; it gives grants and awards to artists in places where culture is under pressure.
princeclaus.money: An annual subsidy from the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

prohelvetia.name: Pro Helvetia
prohelvetia.what: The Swiss Confederation's arts foundation, set up by the Federal Council in 1939 and made a foundation under public law in 1949; based in Zurich.
prohelvetia.money: The Swiss federal budget, set by parliament in four-year Cultural Messages: CHF 186.9 million for 2025 to 2028.
prohelvetia.arts: In 2025 it approved 2,448 of 7,235 applications and put 86.9 percent of its funds directly into art and culture.

provinceofbc|Canada.name: Government of British Columbia
provinceofbc|Canada.what: The provincial government of British Columbia, Canada, led by a Premier and Cabinet answerable to the 93-member Legislative Assembly in Victoria.
provinceofbc|Canada.money: Provincial taxes, natural resource royalties and federal transfers; revenue was forecast at C$83.3 billion for 2025-26.

qatarmuseums.name: Qatar Museums

qatarmuseums.arts: It oversees the Museum of Islamic Art, Mathaf, the National Museum of Qatar and the 3-2-1 Qatar Olympic and Sports Museum.

qattan.name: A. M. Qattan Foundation
qattan.what: A Palestinian non-profit foundation set up in 1993 by the businessman Abdel Mohsin Al-Qattan and based in Ramallah; it is also a registered UK charity.
qattan.money: Donations of £2.02 million and investment income of £484,080 in 2025, of £2.62 million income reported by its UK charity.
qattan.arts: It opened a US$21 million headquarters and arts centre in Ramallah in June 2018.

qattantodate.name: A. M. Qattan Foundation
qattantodate.what: An independent foundation for culture and education in Palestine and the Arab world, set up in 1993 by the Palestinian businessman Abdel Mohsin Al-Qattan and based in Ramallah.

realdania.name: Realdania
realdania.what: A Danish member-based philanthropic association created in 2000, when Realkredit Danmark sold its mortgage business in its merger with Danske Bank, based in Copenhagen.
realdania.money: Returns on investing the capital it kept from that deal; about 195,000 members own it.
realdania.arts: It funds projects in architecture, planning and the built environment.

regionecampania.name: Regione Campania
regionecampania.what: The regional government of Campania in southern Italy, seated in Naples and led by President Roberto Fico with a 60-member Regional Council.

regionelazio.name: Regione Lazio
regionelazio.what: The regional government of Lazio in central Italy, seated in Rome and led by President Francesco Rocca, with a Regional Council as its legislature.
regionelazio.money: The regional budget; its 2025 economic and financial plan set the 2025 to 2027 budget at about EUR 10 billion.

regionepiemonte.name: Regione Piemonte
regionepiemonte.what: The regional government of Piedmont, an Italian region with ordinary statute created in 1948 and operating since 1970; seat in Turin.
regionepiemonte.money: The regional budget, which draws on its own taxes such as IRAP, regional surcharges and car tax.

rgionbourgognefranchecomt.name: Région Bourgogne-Franche-Comté

rgiongrandest.money: Mostly national VAT shared out by the French state (53% of French regions' operating revenue in 2024); its planned 2026 budget is EUR 4.1 billion.

rgionsud.name: Région Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur
rgionsud.what: The regional council of Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, the south-eastern French region also called Région Sud, seated in Marseille.
rgionsud.money: Mainly a share of national VAT assigned by the French state; councillors adopted a EUR 3.2 billion budget for 2024.
rgionsud.arts: The 2024 budget gave EUR 67 million to arts and culture.

right:cohen.name: Steven A. Cohen
right:cohen.what: An American hedge fund manager, founder of Point72 Asset Management (2014, Stamford, Connecticut) and owner of the New York Mets.
right:cohen.money: His hedge fund fortune: S.A.C. Capital Advisors from 1992, which pleaded guilty to insider trading in 2013, then Point72.
right:cohen.arts: The Steven & Alexandra Cohen Foundation, started in 2001, has granted US$1.5 billion to health, education, arts and culture and New York projects.
right:cohen.wrong_match: The Aldrich and NYU Tisch sentences do not name Cohen or Point72; the MOCA sentence records that he left its board.

rolex.name: Rolex SA
rolex.what: A Geneva watchmaker founded in London in 1905 by Hans Wilsdorf and Alfred Davis, owned since 1960 by the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation.
rolex.money: Sales of Rolex and Tudor wristwatches by a company wholly owned by the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation, a private Swiss foundation.
rolex.arts: Its Rolex Mentor and Protégé Arts Initiative, set up in 2002, pairs emerging artists with established ones and gives each protégé about $41,000.

sasktel.name: Saskatchewan Telecommunications Holding Corporation
sasktel.what: A telecommunications Crown corporation owned by the Government of Saskatchewan, founded in 1908 and based in Regina.
sasktel.money: Phone, wireless and internet services, with almost C$1.4 billion of annual revenue and C$104.7 million net income for 2025-26.

sigridrausingtrust.name: The Sigrid Rausing Trust
sigridrausingtrust.what: A London grant-making trust for human rights, open societies and the environment, established in 1995 by Sigrid Rausing.
sigridrausingtrust.money: Funds that Sigrid Rausing, granddaughter of Tetra Pak co-founder Ruben Rausing, moved into it from her Sea Foundation in 1996.

sparebankstiftelsendnb.name: Sparebankstiftelsen DNB
sparebankstiftelsendnb.what: A Norwegian foundation set up in 2002 when Sparebanken NOR became a share company, tracing to Christiania Sparebank of 1822, based in Oslo.
sparebankstiftelsendnb.money: Dividends on its stake of about 8.9% in DNB.
sparebankstiftelsendnb.arts: It buys art shown in Norwegian museums and lends instruments to musicians from a collection begun in 2006.

srp.name: Salt River Project
srp.what: A not-for-profit Arizona utility run by the Salt River Valley Water Users' Association, formed in 1903, and the Salt River Project Agricultural Improvement and Power District.
srp.money: Electricity and water bills from more than 2 million people, including more than 1.2 million electric customers in central Arizona.

statenskunstfond.name: Statens Kunstfond
statenskunstfond.what: Denmark's state arts foundation, set up by law on 27 May 1964 and merged with the Danish Arts Council in 2014, administered by a Ministry of Culture agency.
statenskunstfond.money: Danish state funds allocated by the culture ministry.
statenskunstfond.arts: Its 16 expert committees award grants to more than 6,400 artists and art projects a year from about 15,700 applications.

stateoflowersaxony|Germany.name: Niedersächsisches Ministerium für Wissenschaft und Kultur
stateoflowersaxony|Germany.short: Lower Saxony Ministry for Science and Culture
stateoflowersaxony|Germany.what: The science and culture ministry of the German state of Lower Saxony in Hanover, led since 8 November 2022 by Minister Falko Mohrs.
stateoflowersaxony|Germany.money: The state budget of Lower Saxony.

stavrosniarchos.name: Stavros S. Niarchos Foundation for Charity
stavrosniarchos.what: A philanthropic foundation set up in 1996 after the death of Greek shipping magnate Stavros Niarchos, with offices in Athens, New York and Monaco.
stavrosniarchos.money: An endowment from Stavros Niarchos's shipping fortune; for many years he owned the world's largest private fleet, over 80 tankers and other vessels.
stavrosniarchos.arts: Arts and culture is one of its four grant priorities; since 1996 it has committed nearly $4 billion to grantees in 138 countries.

stichtingdoen.name: Stichting DOEN
stichtingdoen.what: A Dutch foundation set up more than 30 years ago by the Postcode Loterij to fund small, innovative initiatives.
stichtingdoen.money: Lottery proceeds: EUR 24.3 million from the Postcode Loterij and EUR 7.2 million from the VriendenLoterij in 2025.
stichtingdoen.arts: Its VriendenLoterij Fonds funded 70 art and cultural projects in 2025.

swedishartscouncil|Sweden.name: Statens kulturråd
swedishartscouncil|Sweden.what: A Swedish government agency under the Ministry of Culture that distributes state cultural grants, based at Filmhuset in Stockholm.
swedishartscouncil|Sweden.money: Appropriations from the Swedish state budget, set each year in the government's regleringsbrev.

terraforamericanart.name: Terra Foundation for American Art
terraforamericanart.what: A private foundation for American art set up in 1978 by Daniel J. Terra, founder of Lawter Chemicals, with offices in Chicago and Paris.
terraforamericanart.money: An endowment that pays for its grants; its assets were US$582 million in 2020.
terraforamericanart.arts: It closed its Chicago museum in 2004 to give grants and lend its collection; in 2012 it gave US$7.6 million.

thompson.name: The James H.W. Thompson Foundation
thompson.what: A Thai foundation set up in 1976 by the court-appointed administrator of Jim Thompson's property, under the royal patronage of Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn.
thompson.money: Jim Thompson's Bangkok house and art collection, turned over to it in 1976.
thompson.arts: It runs the Jim Thompson Art Center, artist residencies and grants for preserving Thai art and culture.

torontoartscouncil|Canada.name: Toronto Arts Council
torontoartscouncil|Canada.what: Toronto's city-wide public funding body for the arts, created in 1974; a charitable organization working under an arm's-length funding agreement with the City of Toronto.
torontoartscouncil|Canada.money: An annual appropriation from the City of Toronto of about C$25 million.
torontoartscouncil|Canada.address: 26 Grand Trunk Crescent, Suite 200, Toronto, ON M5J 3A9

tunisair.name: Société Tunisienne de l'Air
tunisair.what: Tunisia's national airline, formed by the government in 1948 and based near Tunis-Carthage International Airport.
tunisair.money: Ticket sales, with turnover of TND 1,627 million in 2025; the state holds 64.86% and three state funds 9.56%.

unesco.name: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
unesco.what: A specialised agency of the United Nations founded in 1945, with 194 member states and headquarters in Paris.
unesco.money: Assessed contributions that member states must pay, plus voluntary contributions from governments, international bodies, companies and other donors.

uniqlo.name: Fast Retailing Co., Ltd.
uniqlo.what: A Japanese retail holding company incorporated in 1963 by Hitoshi Yanai, owner of Uniqlo and GU, with its head office in Yamaguchi and an office in Tokyo.
uniqlo.money: Clothing sales, chiefly Uniqlo: revenue of 3.9633 trillion yen in the year to August 2026.

vancleef.name: Van Cleef & Arpels
vancleef.what: A French jewellery house founded in Paris in 1896 by Alfred Van Cleef and Salomon Arpels, owned by the luxury group Richemont since 1999.
vancleef.money: Sales of jewellery through 155 stores, as part of Richemont.

vgc.name: Vlaamse Gemeenschapscommissie
vgc.what: The body that represents the Flemish authorities in the Brussels-Capital Region, created by the special law of 12 January 1989 and answerable to the Flemish Parliament.
vgc.money: A dotation from the Flemish government's budget, EUR 30,588,000 in 2025, plus EUR 1,116,000 a year for community infrastructure.
vgc.arts: It runs more than 20 Dutch-language public libraries, including Muntpunt, and 22 community centres in Brussels.

vriendenloterij.name: VriendenLoterij N.V.
vriendenloterij.what: A Dutch charity lottery company, started in 1989 as the Sponsor Bingo Loterij and renamed in 2011; part of the Holding Nationale Goede Doelen Loterijen.
vriendenloterij.money: Ticket sales to its 1.3 million players; at least 40% of each ticket goes to culture, welfare and sport in the Netherlands.
vriendenloterij.arts: It gave 160 million euros to culture, sport and welfare in 2025.

vsbfonds.name: VSBfonds
vsbfonds.what: A Dutch fund in Utrecht named after the Verenigde Spaarbank (VSB), formed in 1983 from 19th-century Nutsspaarbanken savings banks.
vsbfonds.money: Returns on capital held by Stichting VSB Vermogensfonds, built from the VSB shares the fund owned after the bank merged into Fortis in 1990.

walmart.name: Walmart Inc.
walmart.what: A US retailer founded in 1962 by the brothers Sam and Bud Walton, running Walmart stores and Sam's Club, headquartered in Bentonville, Arkansas.
walmart.money: Retail sales; total revenue was US$713.2 billion in fiscal 2026.

warholfdn.name: The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts
warholfdn.what: A New York nonprofit set up in 1987 under Andy Warhol's will, which also serves as the artist's estate.
warholfdn.money: An endowment built from Warhol's assets, plus income from licensing and selling his works.
warholfdn.arts: It has given more than US$300 million in cash grants to over 1,000 arts organisations in 49 states and abroad.
warholfdn.address: 65 Bleecker Street, 7th Floor, New York, NY 10012

wesfarmersarts.name: Wesfarmers Limited
wesfarmersarts.what: An Australian conglomerate headquartered in Perth, with retail, chemicals, fertiliser, industrial and safety businesses, mainly in Australia and New Zealand.
wesfarmersarts.money: Sales of its businesses, with revenue of A$45.7 billion in the 2025 financial year.
wesfarmersarts.arts: Wesfarmers Arts funds arts groups in Western Australia and nationally and manages the Wesfarmers Collection of Australian Art.
wesfarmersarts.address: Level 14, Brookfield Place Tower 2, 123 St Georges Terrace, Perth WA 6000

wienerstdtische.name: Wiener Städtische Versicherung AG
wienerstdtische.what: An Austrian insurer founded in Vienna in 1824, the largest single company in the Vienna Insurance Group.
wienerstdtische.money: Insurance premiums, about EUR 3,196.2 million gross; the Wiener Städtische Versicherungsverein is the group's main shareholder.

winnipegartscouncil|Canada.name: Winnipeg Arts Council
winnipegartscouncil|Canada.what: A not-for-profit charity that the City of Winnipeg charges with distributing its arts funding and managing its Public Art Policy.
winnipegartscouncil|Canada.money: City arts funding of C$4.65 million in 2025, plus C$258,570 for five city-designated museums.

wolfson.name: The Wolfson Foundation
wolfson.what: A UK grant-making charity set up in 1955 by Isaac Wolfson, chairman of Great Universal Stores, with his wife and son Leonard; based in London.
wolfson.money: Its endowment, just under £1 billion in 2024, when it spent £44 million on charitable activities.

wrth.name: Würth Group
wrth.what: A family-owned German group selling fastening and assembly materials, founded by Adolf Würth in Künzelsau in 1945 and led by his son Reinhold Würth from 1954.
wrth.money: Sales through more than 400 companies in 80 countries, EUR 20.7 billion in 2025.
wrth.arts: Its Kunsthalle Würth reopened in October 2026 for its 25th anniversary.
